transcript:
David: Before Blair starts, here is what you can actually do for these brokers tonight, as of this build. You can pull what every carrier pays in any market in the country, live, on your phone, with the sample size and the date on every number. You can mint a rate exhibit with a broker's own firm name on the cover and hand it to them before the panel ends. You can show a general agency their whole downline's renewals on one register, with a clock counting down on every group. You can open the drug ledger and show a self-funded employer what each drug costs to acquire, what the plan was billed, and who kept the rebate. And you can show the paid claim next to the filed contract, side by side on one screen. And when someone asks what it costs, the first look is free, no card. A seat is one hundred forty nine a month. The whole firm is forty nine hundred a year, flat. If they want it live on their own book, that is a twenty minute call. That is the toolkit. Now the questions.

Blair: You keep saying the villain is a file. Not a carrier. Not a person. A file.

David: Right. Most health plans have to file the rates they've agreed to. Those files are public. They're also huge. Almost nobody on the buying side ever opens one. There's no villain in that. It's just a file nobody opens.
